audit_findings.title: The anchor may capitalize a legally unsettled tariff shock as permanent
audit_findings.magnitude: $16.0 million of 2025 incremental tariffs, equal to 73.7% of the $21.7 million anchor; subsequently filed recoveries include $15.3 million credited to cost of sales, $3.3 million credited to inventory, and $0.7 million of interest
audit_findings.mechanism: The unadjusted tariff expense depresses anchor OE and every forecast year, while any refund belongs once in the bridge or as a nonrecurring receipt rather than recurring OE; replacement tariffs affect normalized margins and growth.
audit_findings.evidence: We paid approximately $16 million of incremental tariffs in 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated change in the economics underlying the anchor, not merely a hypothetical risk. The June filing confirms substantial approval and recognition of refunds, but the recurring burden under the replacement 10% and later 12.5% tariffs remains uncertain. Because the original tariff cost was nearly three-quarters of anchor OE, normalization can materially change operating value in either direction relative to an incorrectly chosen recurring tariff burden.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $16.0 million paid in 2025 to the $15.3 million P&L recovery and $3.3 million inventory adjustment, isolate amounts attributable to 2025 sales, estimate recurring replacement-tariff costs after pricing mitigation, and rerun all scenarios while including the refund receivable or subsequent cash exactly once.

audit_findings.title: The bridge may treat operating cash as fully distributable excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; the exposed bridge balance is $95.471 million, with $30.2 million of filed purchase commitments, $5.3 million of foreign cash, and a computed planned inventory rebuild of approximately $20.9 million from $49.069 million to about $70 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Any minimum operating-cash requirement must be withheld from the cash-and-short-term-investments bridge rather than added to equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025, we had commitments to purchase $ 30.2 million of inventory, all of which were due in less than one year.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings establish meaningful working-capital demands but do not establish the minimum cash reserve or how much of the purchase commitments will be funded by payables and operating inflows. The planned $20.9 million inventory rebuild alone equals about $2.06 per diluted share, but it is not a defensible proxy for the complete reserve. Materiality therefore remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Build a monthly cash and working-capital schedule through the seasonal inventory peak, reconcile purchase commitments to payables and expected collections, identify legally or operationally restricted foreign cash, and rerun the bridge using only demonstrably excess cash.

audit_findings.title: An unfunded pension claim ahead of common equity is not shown in the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $8.077 million net unfunded obligation at December 31, 2025, computed as the $11.334 million supplemental-plan deficit less the $3.257 million qualified-plan surplus; approximately $0.79 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: A pre-existing pension claim reduces the equity bridge unless its settlement cash flows are explicitly and fully deducted in forecast OE; the qualified-plan surplus offsets part of the supplemental-plan deficit.
audit_findings.evidence: Our unfunded benefit obligation was $8.1 million and $10.4 million at December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The pension claim and its omission from the stated bridge are demonstrated, although the degree already represented by pension costs in OE requires reconciliation. Deducting the full filed net obligation would reduce base value from $39.38 to about $38.59 per share and bull value from $42.88 to about $42.09, both still below the $45.37 market price. It therefore does not change the valuation conclusion on the filed scale.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the June 2026 current and long-term supplemental liabilities and qualified-plan surplus, incorporate the authorized qualified-plan termination, and confirm that projected supplemental payments are either deducted in the bridge or explicitly modeled in OE without double counting.

audit_findings.title: Company-owned life insurance may create numerator–bridge incoherence
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed reference amounts are $22.147 million of cash-surrender value, a $23.3 million death benefit, a $0.841 million 2025 noncash increase, and a $0.240 million increase during the first half of 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Noncash cash-value accretion should be removed from OE if it is not distributable operating cash, while the realizable policy asset may belong in the bridge net of taxes and associated benefit obligations.
audit_findings.evidence: Upon death of the insured executives, the approximate benefit we would receive is $ 23.3 million in aggregate as of December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The asset and noncash accretion are demonstrated, but the supplied OE calculation does not show whether the accretion was purged, and the record does not establish realizable proceeds, tax leakage, or the portion economically supporting executive benefits. Adding the entire filed carrying value would equal about $2.18 per share, while purging capitalized accretion would move value in the opposite direction. The net materiality cannot be established from the record.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $0.841 million increase through net income and the OE adjustments, obtain the current policy cash-surrender value and surrender-tax basis, identify any policy restrictions or benefit linkage, and rerun OE and the bridge using one coherent net treatment.

audit_findings.title: A noncash tax valuation allowance may remain in the latest-year anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.541 million 2025 tax charge, equal to 7.1% of the $21.7 million anchor; if fully retained, the computed base operating-value effect is approximately $21.7 million or $2.13 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: A noncash valuation-allowance charge retained in anchor OE depresses every forecast year even though it is not a current cash tax payment.
audit_findings.evidence: The 2025 effective tax rate differed from the U.S. federal statutory rate of 21% because of state taxes and the establishment of a valuation allowance on Florsheim Australia’s deferred tax assets.
audit_findings.explanation: The $1.541 million charge is filed, but whether it remains in the OE anchor is unresolved. Even assuming the entire charge is erroneously retained and scaling each scenario's operating PV proportionally, base value would rise only to about $41.51 per share and bull value to about $45.26, still below the $45.37 market price. The buy-below level would rise to roughly $29.06, also well below the market price, so the standalone issue does not change the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $1.541 million valuation-allowance charge through the OE calculation, remove it if retained, preserve only supportable recurring cash taxes, and document that no benefit from the Australian loss carryforwards is recognized prematurely.

audit_findings.title: A LIFO liquidation benefit modestly inflated the anchor year
audit_findings.magnitude: $0.3 million pre-tax, or approximately $0.216 million after applying the filed 28.0% effective tax rate; computed base-value effect is about $0.30 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: The liquidation benefit reduced 2025 cost of sales and therefore increased anchor OE despite arising from older inventory layers rather than current operating economics.
audit_findings.evidence: During 2025, there were liquidations of LIFO inventory quantities carried at lower costs prevailing in prior years compared to the cost of fiscal 2025 purchases; the effect of these liquidations decreased cost of sales by $ 0.3 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The nonrecurring benefit is demonstrated. If fully retained in OE, removing its estimated after-tax effect would lower base value from $39.38 to about $39.08 per share and bull value from $42.88 to about $42.55, leaving the valuation conclusion unchanged relative to the $45.37 market price.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether the $0.3 million pre-tax benefit was normalized out; if not, remove its after-tax effect from anchor OE and rerun the scenarios.
